What I Built

Last week I ran du -sh ~/Downloads on my laptop and realized I was hoarding hundreds of cryptic PDFs (INV-9041-final(1).pdf), forgotten .exe installers, and unnamed screenshots—and I refused to upload my private bank receipts or .env configs to a cloud AI just to sort them. So for International Sloth Day, I built a daemon that waits until I walk away from my keyboard and cleans the mess locally while I sleep.

Workspaces, Desktop dumps, and project inboxes are where good intentions go to hibernate. Cryptic filenames pile up (Screenshot 2026-10-18 at 2.34.12 PM.png, INV-9041-final(1).pdf, DockerDesktopInstaller.exe). Receipts, strategy documents, archives, and configuration files end up in a flat, unorganized heap because standard file extensions tell you almost nothing about what a document actually contains.

I built slothd, a local-first, offline-capable AI file organizer designed around the philosophy of "Slow and Steady":

  • Patient Idle Activation: Uses native OS APIs to measure keyboard and mouse inactivity. It sleeps while you work and only activates when you step away.
  • Two-Stage Intelligence Funnel: Fast metadata triage (1ms via local 7-signal engine, ~20ms via Prior Labs TabPFN) flags anomalies (clutter, stale installers, duplicate hashes) before invoking heavier models.
  • Local Vision & Text Comprehension: Uses Gemma 3 running locally in Ollama with strict Pydantic JSON schemas to read PDFs, invoices, and images.
  • Natural Language Semantic Search: Embeds organized files into Tiger Data pgvector (768-dim nomic-embed-text) with a local SQLite vector fallback, enabling queries like "Where is my AWS invoice from October?".
  • Non-Destructive & Reversible: Every run is a dry-run by default. Every approved move is written to an SQLite WAL log with a unique batch ID. If you dislike what it did, slothd undo restores every file to its exact original path.
  • Glassmorphic Local Dashboard: A lightweight, dependency-free web UI (FastAPI + Vanilla ES6) with live stats, move manifest inspector, interactive activity timeline, and an ElevenLabs audio briefing player.

🔒 Local-First & Air-Gapped by Default: The entire core workflow—idle detection, filesystem scanning, tabular metadata triage, Gemma 3 document understanding via local Ollama, SQLite WAL manifests, and 1-click rollback—executes 100% locally on your machine with zero internet calls. A genuinely air-gapped deployment simply leaves external integrations disabled. Cloud partner services (Tiger Data pgvector, SerpApi vendor lookup, ElevenLabs voice) are strictly opt-in extensions via explicit CLI flags (--enrich-online), and each is engineered with a complete offline fallback (local SQLite vector search, local heuristics, terminal audio chimes). No personal file or metadata ever leaves your device by default.

Who gets to be a little lazier because of it?

Every developer, creator, and researcher who wastes 20 minutes every week digging through unorganized files, manually dragging PDFs into dated folders, or putting off digital cleanup. You let the sloth run patiently while you make coffee, return to an inspected plan, and keep complete control.

The Offline Demo Fixture: Reproduce in 10 Seconds

You don't need to risk your own files to evaluate slothd. The repository includes a deterministic test fixture in test_workspace/messy_inbox containing an invoice, duplicate invoice, Uber receipt, project notes, Python benchmark, configuration file, leftover Windows installer, stale zip archive, and unsorted screenshots.

Anyone can clone and run the scan immediately:

git clone https://github.com/JaniDhruv/slothd.git
cd slothd
uv run slothd scan test_workspace/messy_inbox

In under a second, you will observe the verified metrics:

  • 10 files scanned
  • 2 clutter anomalies flagged in 1 ms (via deterministic 7-feature triage engine / TabPFN schema)
  • 1 exact duplicate set detected via SHA-256 (973 B reclaimable)
  • 0 cloud API calls required (100% air-gapped isolation)

How I Built It

A file organizer that feeds every single file into a heavy vision model is noisy, slow, and expensive. Instead, slothd uses a structured two-stage funnel:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Messy Target Directory                   │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
              1. Deduplicate & Extract Features
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│     STAGE 1: Prior Labs TabPFN Metadata Triage         │
│  (7 tabular signals: log size, depth, ext, time, etc.) │
└─────────────┬────────────────────────────┬─────────────┘
              │                            │
   Leftover installers, archives,          │ Needs deeper
   screenshots, duplicate clutter          │ semantic classification
              ▼                            ▼
   Flagged for cleanup          ┌────────────────────────┐
                                │ STAGE 2: Gemma 3 Local │
                                │   (Ollama Vision/Text) │
                                └──────────┬─────────────┘
                                           │
                                           ▼
                                ┌────────────────────────┐
                                │ SQLite Reversible Log  │
                                │  + Tiger Data pgvector │
                                └────────────────────────┘

Stage 1: Lightweight Tabular Triage (Prior Labs TabPFN)

Before running AI models, slothd extracts 7 tabular signals from the filesystem:

  1. Log-scaled file size
  2. Extension category group
  3. Path depth
  4. Hour of modification
  5. Day of week
  6. Filename length
  7. Numeric/UUID entropy signal

When TabPFN credentials or a local model checkpoint are configured, TabPFN evaluates these tabular feature distributions directly (taking ~15–25 ms). To guarantee strict zero-credential, air-gapped operation by default, slothd also bundles a calibrated deterministic heuristic engine (TabPFN-Heuristic-Local) that evaluates the exact same 7-signal feature vector in under 1 millisecond.

(Note on benchmark accuracy: The 1 ms timing reported in the deterministic test fixture reflects this local offline heuristic engine. When running against TabPFN's hosted model with credentials, inference takes ~20 ms across the batch. Both modes share the exact same Pydantic triage interface and 100% test pass rate).

Stage 2: Local Vision & Content Understanding (Gemma 3)

Only files requiring semantic classification (unlabeled PDFs, scanned receipts, documents) are forwarded to local Gemma 3 via Ollama.

  • PDFs are converted to in-memory images via PyMuPDF.
  • Outputs are constrained via Pydantic schema passed directly to Ollama's format parameter. The model output is validated token-by-token at the grammar level: category, subcategory, description, date, vendor, proposed_name, confidence, and tags.
  • If Ollama is offline, a 0.2s health probe triggers an instant fallback to local extension classification, preventing the CLI from ever freezing.

Safe, Non-Destructive File Operations

The organization pipeline enforces strict safety invariants:

  1. Non-Destructive Dry Run: slothd organize prints the plan without moving files. You must explicitly pass --go or click "Approve" in the dashboard.
  2. Collision Avoidance: If Invoices/AWS_Invoice_2026.pdf already exists, slothd automatically appends _1, _2 instead of overwriting.
  3. Timestamp Preservation: Original modification times (mtime, atime) are preserved on moved files.
  4. SQLite WAL Manifest: Every operation logs batch_id, old_path, new_path, and timestamp.
  5. Instant Rollback: Running slothd undo restores the entire batch in reverse order.

Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

Personal files contain our most vulnerable data:

  • Tax returns and bank statements
  • Medical lab reports and health records
  • Invoices and payment receipts
  • Confidential code and configuration secrets

Uploading this stream of daily life to closed, centralized cloud APIs creates an unacceptable privacy tradeoff.

Open-weight AI (Gemma 3) and open-source tabular models (TabPFN) fundamentally change this dynamic. They make it possible to run state-of-the-art vision and tabular triage entirely inside the boundary of your own computer:

  • No document crosses your local network without explicit opt-in.
  • Models can be audited, swapped, or operated air-gapped without internet access.
  • Partner integrations (SerpApi online vendor grounding, ElevenLabs voice) require explicit flags (--enrich-online) and are never enabled by default.

Privacy is not a checkbox added after the architecture is done; with open-source AI, privacy is the architecture.

The Lazy Payoff

The lazy payoff is not about moving files a few milliseconds faster. It is about removing the cognitive dread of manual digital housekeeping.

Instead of spending Sunday afternoon opening dozens of PDFs one by one, deciphering cryptic filenames, and deciding where each document belongs:

  1. You let slothd daemon run in the background.
  2. It detects when you step away from your keyboard.
  3. It spots clutter anomalies and duplicates in 1 millisecond (via local tabular triage).
  4. It reads invoices and dates with Gemma 3.
  5. You return to a tidy proposed plan, hit enter to approve, and know that every single change can be undone with slothd undo.

1. 🦥 Grand Prize: Hacktoberfest Week 3 "Slow and Steady"

  • Concept: Embodying International Sloth Day with native OS idle measurement (Win32 GetLastInputInfo, macOS IOHIDSystem, Linux xprintidle) that sleeps during work and activates only after 5+ minutes of continuous inactivity. All actions are dry-run by default and 100% reversible via SQLite WAL manifests.

2. 💎 Featured Track: Best Use of Gemma

  • Module: slothd/engine/classifier.py
  • Design: Deep local document comprehension using gemma3:4b running in Ollama. PyMuPDF renders PDF pages in-memory for visual token ingestion, constrained token-by-token with strict Pydantic JSON grammar schemas to eliminate hallucinations.

3. 📊 Featured Track: Best Use of TabPFN

  • Module: slothd/engine/tabular_predictor.py
  • Design: Operates as Stage 1 in the prediction agent funnel. Evaluates 7 filesystem numerical distributions in under 1 ms (local heuristic fallback) or ~20 ms (TabPFN model) to flag anomalies and installer clutter before LLM activation. Covered in tests/test_tabular_predictor.py.

4. 🐯 Partner Track: Best Use of Tiger Data

  • Module: slothd/engine/search.py & slothd/integrations/tiger_data.py
  • Design: Stores 768-dimensional nomic-embed-text embeddings in Tiger Data PostgreSQL with pgvector IVFFlat cosine distance indexing (<=>), backed by an automatic local SQLite vector fallback.

5. 🔭 Partner Track: Best Use of Sentry Agent Tracing

  • Module: slothd/integrations/sentry_tracing.py
  • Design: Distributed span tracing across scanner, AI triage, and execution boundaries. Verified with authentic production traces (Issue #7805015409, trace_id: 71ac0b2ff1dc4c4788ff6a5b7098e354) that resolved three real development regressions (3a327ea, a914b53, df19f29).

6. 🔍 Partner Track: Best Use of SerpApi

  • Module: slothd/integrations/serpapi_client.py
  • Design: Opt-in --enrich-online live web grounding for mysterious software names and vendor IDs, locally cached with zero transmission of private document bodies.

7. 🎙️ Partner Track: Best Use of ElevenLabs

  • Module: slothd/integrations/elevenlabs.py
  • Design: Sloan the Sloth witty audio summaries via eleven_multilingual_v2 (slothd briefing), featuring local offline chime fallbacks when no API key is configured.

8. 🤖 Partner Track: Best Use of GitHub Copilot

  • Module: .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/prompts/, and slothd/cli.py
  • Design: Authoritative 85-line repository guide, 3 custom prompt templates (/new-sorter, /audit-privacy, /verify-demo), CLI prompt inspector (slothd copilot), and cross-OS CI matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml).

9. 📦 Partner Track: Best Use of Entire

  • Module: .entire/settings.json & .agents/hooks.json
  • Design: Integrates Entire CLI 0.11.6 to maintain immutable agent session provenance, tool checkpoints, and commit logs directly in version control.

Verification & Testing

Every test runs in total offline isolation (no live external services required):

uv run pytest -v
# 118 passed in 40.87s

uv run ruff check .
# All checks passed!

🦥 Parting Sloth Thoughts: Reclaiming Digital Calm

We spend so much time micromanaging our digital clutter—manually dragging files into folders, hunting for lost receipts, or feeling guilty about a desktop covered in final_v2_really_final.pdf.

slothd was built on a very simple premise: your machine should quietly work for you when you're resting, not steal your attention when you're busy.

By embracing open-weights, deterministic rule fallbacks, and respectful idle scheduling, you don't have to surrender your personal documents to cloud silos or burn your laptop's battery just to keep a clean workspace. Take a breath, close your laptop lid, and let the sloth do the heavy lifting while you take a break.

Why Does Open Innovation Matter? Personal files contain our most vulnerable data: Tax returns and bank statements Medical lab reports and health records Invoices and payment receipts Confidential code and configuration secrets Uploading this stream of daily life to closed, centralized cloud APIs creates an unacceptable privacy tradeoff. Open-weight AI (Gemma 3) and open-source tabular models (TabPFN) fundamentally change this dynamic. They make it possible to run state-of-the-art vision and tabular triage entirely inside the boundary of your own computer: No document crosses your local network without explicit opt-in. Models can be audited, swapped, or operated air-gapped without internet access. Partner integrations (SerpApi online vendor grounding, ElevenLabs voice) require explicit flags (--enrich-online) and are never enabled by default. Privacy is not a checkbox added after the architecture is done; with open-source AI, privacy is the architecture. The Lazy Payoff The lazy payoff is not about moving files a few milliseconds faster. It is about removing the cognitive dread of manual digital housekeeping. Instead of spending Sunday afternoon opening dozens of PDFs one by one, deciphering cryptic filenames, and deciding where each document belongs: You let slothd daemon run in the background. It detects when you step away from your keyboard. It spots clutter anomalies and duplicates in 1 millisecond (via local tabular triage). It reads invoices and dates with Gemma 3. You return to a tidy proposed plan, hit enter to approve, and know that every single change can be undone with slothd undo. 我建造了什么

Last week I ran du -sh ~/Downloads on my laptop and realized I was hoarding hundreds of cryptic PDFs (INV-9041-final(1).pdf), forgotten .exe installers, and unnamed screenshots—and I refused to upload my private bank receipts or .env configs to a cloud AI just to sort them. So for International Sloth Day, I built a daemon that waits until I walk away from my keyboard and cleans the mess locally while I sleep.

Workspaces, Desktop dumps, and project inboxes are where good intentions go to hibernate. Cryptic filenames pile up (Screenshot 2026-10-18 at 2.34.12 PM.png, INV-9041-final(1).pdf, DockerDesktopInstaller.exe). Receipts, strategy documents, archives, and configuration files end up in a flat, unorganized heap because standard file extensions tell you almost nothing about what a document actually contains.

I built slothd, a local-first, offline-capable AI file organizer designed around the philosophy of "Slow and Steady":

  • Patient Idle Activation: Uses native OS APIs to measure keyboard and mouse inactivity. It sleeps while you work and only activates when you step away.
  • Two-Stage Intelligence Funnel: Fast metadata triage (1ms via local 7-signal engine, ~20ms via Prior Labs TabPFN) flags anomalies (clutter, stale installers, duplicate hashes) before invoking heavier models.
  • Local Vision & Text Comprehension: Uses Gemma 3 running locally in Ollama with strict Pydantic JSON schemas to read PDFs, invoices, and images.
  • Natural Language Semantic Search: Embeds organized files into Tiger Data pgvector (768-dim nomic-embed-text) with a local SQLite vector fallback, enabling queries like "Where is my AWS invoice from October?".
  • Non-Destructive & Reversible: Every run is a dry-run by default. Every approved move is written to an SQLite WAL log with a unique batch ID. If you dislike what it did, slothd undo restores every file to its exact original path.
  • Glassmorphic Local Dashboard: A lightweight, dependency-free web UI (FastAPI + Vanilla ES6) with live stats, move manifest inspector, interactive activity timeline, and an ElevenLabs audio briefing player.
🔒 Local-First & Air-Gapped by Default: The entire core workflow—idle detection, filesystem scanning, tabular metadata triage, Gemma 3 document understanding via local Ollama, SQLite WAL manifests, and 1-click rollback—executes 100% locally on your machine with zero internet calls. A genuinely air-gapped deployment simply leaves external integrations disabled. Cloud partner services (Tiger Data pgvector, SerpApi vendor lookup, ElevenLabs voice) are strictly opt-in extensions via explicit CLI flags (--enrich-online), and each is engineered with a complete offline fallback (local SQLite vector search, local heuristics, terminal audio chimes). No personal file or metadata ever leaves your device by default.

Who gets to be a little lazier because of it?

Every developer, creator, and researcher who wastes 20 minutes every week digging through unorganized files, manually dragging PDFs into dated folders, or putting off digital cleanup. You let the sloth run patiently while you make coffee, return to an inspected plan, and keep complete control.

Demo

The complete interactive loop demonstrates the full lifecycle:

Messy Workspace 
  ➜ Fast Metadata Triage (TabPFN / Local Heuristic) 
  ➜ Local AI Plan (Gemma 3) 
  ➜ Dry-Run Preview

Stage 1: Lightweight Tabular Triage (Prior Labs TabPFN)

Before running AI models, slothd extracts 7 tabular signals from the filesystem:

  1. Log-scaled file size
  2. Extension category group
  3. Path depth
  4. Hour of modification
  5. Day of week
  6. Filename length
  7. Numeric/UUID entropy signal

When TabPFN credentials or a local model checkpoint are configured, TabPFN evaluates these tabular feature distributions directly (taking ~15–25 ms). To guarantee strict zero-credential, air-gapped operation by default, slothd also bundles a calibrated deterministic heuristic engine (TabPFN-Heuristic-Local) that evaluates the exact same 7-signal feature vector in under 1 millisecond.

(Note on benchmark accuracy: The 1 ms timing reported in the deterministic test fixture reflects this local offline heuristic engine. When running against TabPFN's hosted model with credentials, inference takes ~20 ms across the batch. Both modes share the exact same Pydantic triage interface and 100% test pass rate).

Stage 2: Local Vision & Content Understanding (Gemma 3)

Only files requiring semantic classification (unlabeled PDFs, scanned receipts, documents) are forwarded to local Gemma 3 via Ollama.

  • PDFs are converted to in-memory images via PyMuPDF.
  • Outputs are constrained via Pydantic schema passed directly to Ollama's format parameter. The model output is validated token-by-token at the grammar level: category, subcategory, description, date, vendor, proposed_name, confidence, and tags.
  • If Ollama is offline, a 0.2s health probe triggers an instant fallback to local extension classification, preventing the CLI from ever freezing.

Safe, Non-Destructive File Operations

The organization pipeline enforces strict safety invariants:

  1. Non-Destructive Dry Run: slothd organize prints the plan without moving files. You must explicitly pass --go or click "Approve" in the dashboard.
  2. Collision Avoidance: If Invoices/AWS_Invoice_2026.pdf already exists, slothd automatically appends _1, _2 instead of overwriting.
  3. Timestamp Preservation: Original modification times (mtime, atime) are preserved on moved files.
  4. SQLite WAL Manifest: Every operation logs batch_id, old_path, new_path, and timestamp.
  5. Instant Rollback: Running slothd undo restores the entire batch in reverse order.

Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

Personal files contain our most vulnerable data:

  • Tax returns and bank statements
  • Medical lab reports and health records
  • Invoices and payment receipts
  • Confidential code and configuration secrets

Uploading this stream of daily life to closed, centralized cloud APIs creates an unacceptable privacy tradeoff.

Open-weight AI (Gemma 3) and open-source tabular models (TabPFN) fundamentally change this dynamic. They make it possible to run state-of-the-art vision and tabular triage entirely inside the boundary of your own computer:

  • No document crosses your local network without explicit opt-in.
  • Models can be audited, swapped, or operated air-gapped without internet access.
  • Partner integrations (SerpApi online vendor grounding, ElevenLabs voice) require explicit flags (--enrich-online) and are never enabled by default.

Privacy is not a checkbox added after the architecture is done; with open-source AI, privacy is the architecture.

The lazy payoff is not about moving files a few milliseconds faster. It is about removing the cognitive dread of manual digital housekeeping.

Instead of spending Sunday afternoon opening dozens of PDFs one by one, deciphering cryptic filenames, and deciding where each document belongs:
